name: Google-Pinpoint
follows_en: Partial. Google says user-triggered fetchers generally ignore robots.txt rules because a user requested the fetch.

ips.note: Google says user-triggered fetchers publish IP ranges in user-triggered-fetchers.json, user-triggered-fetchers-google.json and user-triggered-agents.json, and that the reverse DNS mask matches ***-***-***-***.gae.googleusercontent.com or google-proxy-***-***-***-***.google.com depending on whether the fetcher is Google or user owned.

vendor_quote: The Google-Pinpoint fetcher requests individual URLs that Pinpoint users specified as sources for their personal collections of documents.

vendor_quote_source.title: Google Search Central: Google user-triggered fetchers

what_en: Google-Pinpoint is a user-triggered fetcher listed by Google. It requests individual URLs that Pinpoint users specified as sources for their personal collections of documents. Google lists it with the user agent Google-Pinpoint.
block_en: Google says that because the fetch was requested by a user, user-triggered fetchers generally ignore robots.txt rules. The Google page documents no robots.txt token for Google-Pinpoint.
compare_en: Both fetch URLs that users supplied as sources in a Google product, and both fall under Google's user-triggered fetcher rules.

sources.title: Google Search Central: Google user-triggered fetchers
Google Search Central: Overview of Google crawlers and fetchers

notes: Google does not say which of the three user-triggered JSON files covers Pinpoint, so no IP count. Google's page does not call it an AI crawler. The token is shown as the HTTP user agent; no robots.txt token is documented.
answer_en: Google-Pinpoint is a user-triggered fetcher listed by Google. It requests individual URLs that Pinpoint users specified as sources for their personal collections of documents. Google says user-triggered fetchers generally ignore robots.txt rules because a user requested the fetch, and documents no robots.txt token for it.
